payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in this chemistry. An independent Halvorsen-Pike audit superseded and retracted the initial cycle-life claim, establishing 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee under controlled accelerated testing. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to be suspended in colder conditions.
